Three laws stated with no premise about the unfolding rest on the same least unit, since each sums falls of at least one: finitely many conditions that keep falling keep rising (`rising_recurs`), an amount that never rises cannot keep falling (`falls_not_recurring`), and joint excess cannot outlast what was held (`Flow.excess_bounded`). 停息定理（`World.comes_to_rest_unrefuted`、`World.rests_unrefuted_enclosed`、`World.rests_unrefuted`）与从外供给（`Flow.fed_from_beyond`）用到这一点：量取实数时损失可以几何地缩小，这些结论不成立；第二定律不给每步的最小损失。三条不加关于展开之前提而陈述的规律也依于同一最小单位，因为每条都把至少为一的下降相加：有限多个条件持续下降就持续上升（`rising_recurs`），不再上升的量不能持续下降（`falls_not_recurring`），联合超出持续不过原有的（`Flow.excess_bounded`）。在稠密的量中，每步减半的存量永远下降而从不上升（`Halving.approaches_without_reaching`）；它们的一般形式是最小损失之律（`Amounts.rests`），`falls_not_recurring` 由它再证（`whole_falls_not_recurring`） |

Amounts do not go below zero, so in a finite family recurring falls need recurring rises: in every unfolding, finitely many conditions that keep falling keep rising; with amounts bounded, recurring rises also need recurring falls.

Amounts are natural numbers, so each fall is at least one unit and none goes below zero; so in a finite family recurring falls need recurring rises: in every unfolding so represented, finitely many conditions that keep falling keep rising (`rising_recurs`). That is a fact of the least unit, not of every unfolding: over dense amounts a stock halving at every step falls for ever and never rises (`Halving.approaches_without_reaching`; block A, natural-number amounts). With amounts bounded, recurring rises also need recurring falls.

**One principle bounds continuation without renewal: an observable that never rises from some step on cannot keep falling.** In Lean: given a rank that does not rise from step T on, it is not the case that the rank falls at steps as late as one likes (`falls_not_recurring`). Three bounds are cases of it:

**One principle bounds continuation without renewal: an amount counted in whole units that never rises from some step on cannot keep falling.** In Lean: given a rank that does not rise from step T on, it is not the case that the rank falls at steps as late as one likes (`falls_not_recurring`). It is a fact of natural-number amounts, where each fall is at least one unit: over dense amounts a stock halving at every step never rises and falls for ever (`Halving.approaches_without_reaching`). Its general form is the least-loss law: falls of at least a least loss, from a stock within finitely many of them, do not recur (`Amounts.rests`); `falls_not_recurring` is that law at whole numbers, proved again from it with its statement unchanged (`whole_falls_not_recurring`; “Limits of the rest theorem” above). Three bounds are cases of it:

Each step of joint excess lowers the level by at least one, so joint excess cannot outlast what was held (`Flow.excess_bounded`).

Each step of joint excess lowers the level by at least one unit, so with natural-number amounts joint excess cannot outlast what was held (`Flow.excess_bounded`: `n` steps of it lower the level by at least `n`). The bound counts each step's excess as at least one unit; over amounts that may be dense it would need a least excess per step, as rest needs a least loss (`Becoming.LeastLoss`).
